text: elevation argument add_outflows() specifies depth outlet withdraws water: Set elevation = -1 (elevation = list(outflow = -1) named list) surface outlet – outlet always withdraws current water surface. title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: General Lake Model (GLM) one-dimensional (1-D), variable-layer hydrodynamic model lakes, reservoirs, estuaries. Originally described Hipsey et al. (2019), GLM simulates vertical profiles temperature, salinity, density driven surface heat exchange, shortwave radiation, wind mixing, inflows, outflows. key architectural features include: Variable-thickness layer scheme — layers merge split dynamically, giving high resolution needed (near thermocline) coarser resolution elsewhere. Flexible inflow/outflow — supports multiple rivers, surface spillways, subsurface outlets arbitrary elevations. Rich surface heat-flux options — sensible heat, latent heat, longwave, shortwave radiation computed standard meteorological inputs. Sediment heat exchange — allows depth-varying bed temperatures drive conductive heat flux water column. detailed GLM documentation available GLM website, Source code: :github: https://github.com/AquaticEcoDynamics/GLM/tree/master Binaries: :github: https://github.com/AquaticEcoDynamics/Binaries

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: Hipsey, M.R., Bruce, L.C., Boon, C., Busch, B., Carey, C.C., Hamilton, D.P., Hanson, P.C., Read, J.S., de Sousa, E., Weber, M. & Winslow, L.. (2019). General Lake Model (GLM 3.0) linking high-frequency sensor data Global Lake Ecological Observatory Network (GLEON). Geoscientific Model Development, 12, 473–523. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-12-473-2019

text: get_model_controls() returns data frame governs biogeochemical variables simulated initialised. Pass use_bgc = TRUE enable full suite water-quality variables. can narrow set simulated variables using set_vars_sim():

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: build model directory called aeme, build_aeme() translates AEME object configuration files required GLM-AED. Setting use_bgc = TRUE writes aed/aed.nml file supporting CSV parameter files phytoplankton, zooplankton, macrophytes. configuration files stored configuration slot aeme object. GLM-AED slot contains parsed glm3.nml aed/aed.nml:
code: path <- "aeme" model <- "glm_aed"  aeme <- build_aeme(   aeme           = aeme,   model          = model,   path           = path,   model_controls = model_controls,   ext_elev       = 3,   use_bgc        = TRUE ) cfg <- configuration(aeme) names(cfg[["glm_aed"]]) #> [1] "hydrodynamic" "bgc"

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: default, AED modules enabled. set_glm_aed_models() lets choose subset — example, running hydrodynamics coupled oxygen nutrient cycling , without phytoplankton zooplankton: run minimal simulation oxygen nutrient cycling:

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: One important GLM-AED features water-quality simulation depth-varying sediment parameters. GLM divides lake bed sediment zones, temperature regime (using aed_sedflux Constant2d mode) sediment–water interface fluxes oxygen nutrients. Deeper zones typically accumulate organic matter, experience longer periods anoxia, therefore higher sediment oxygen demand (SOD) nutrient release shallow littoral zones.

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: estimate_zone_fluxes() scales literature-baseline sediment fluxes zone according mean depth bed-area fraction (Tier 1). observed near-bed concentrations available aeme object, optional Tier 2 adjustment refines inter-zone ratios using summer near-bottom data: zone summary shows zone’s depth range, bed area, estimated fluxes:
code: fluxes <- estimate_zone_fluxes(   aeme      = aeme,   path      = path,   baseline  = c(     fsed_oxy = -25,   # mmol O2/m2/d  (negative = into sediment)     fsed_amm =   2,   # mmol N/m2/d     fsed_nit =   0.2, # mmol N/m2/d     fsed_frp =   0.05 # mmol P/m2/d   ),   verbose   = TRUE ) fluxes$zone_summary #>       zone height_lower_m height_upper_m depth_upper_m depth_lower_m #> Zone1    1           0.00           3.07            10         13.07 #> Zone2    2           3.07          22.00             0         10.00 #>       mean_depth_m area_m2 area_frac fsed_oxy fsed_amm fsed_nit fsed_frp #> Zone1        11.54   43957     0.289    -38.8    5.835     -0.4   0.1035 #> Zone2         5.00  108386     0.711    -19.4    0.512      0.1   0.0259

text: run_glm_aed_diagnostics() reads model output produces structured diagnostic report — summary table set grouped plots — helps quickly identify unrealistic values mass-balance issues:  function returns list three components: $summary — data frame min, median, mean, max, flag column ("ok" warning string) variable. $plots — named list patchwork plot objects grouped biogeochemical element (O, N, P, Phy, Sed). $data — tidy data frame used produce plots. can filter diagnostics specific element type:

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: vignette demonstrated key GLM-AED-specific features available AEME: Model description — GLM provides variable-layer 1-D hydrodynamics; AED supplies modular biogeochemistry ranging simple oxygen dynamics full nutrient–phytoplankton food-web simulation. Module selection — set_glm_aed_models() lets enable disable individual AED modules match complexity data requirements application. Sediment zones — estimate_sed_zones() → glm_sed_params() → set_aed_sed_const2d() workflow automatically derives depth-varying sediment parameters lake hypsograph optional near-bed observations. Configuration visualisation — plot_glm_config() provides interactive overview model setup. Diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics() plot_glm_diagnostics() offer structured, automated checks common biogeochemical issues (unrealistic concentrations, oxygen anomalies, excessive negligible fluxes). Parameter access — get_aeme_parameters() makes easy explore modify individual model parameters manual tuning automated calibration (see aemetools package).

title: Introduction to AEME
text: AEME package hosts three one-dimensional hydrodynamic models: DYnamic REservoir Simulation Model (DYRESM), General Lake Model (GLM), General Ocean Turbulence Model (GOTM, adapted closed basins application lakes reservoirs). models can coupled corresponding water quality models, DYRESM-CAEDYM (Computational Aquatic Ecosystem Dynamics Model), GLM-AED (Aquatic Ecosystem Dynamics Model), GOTM-WET (Water Ecosystem Tool). Key aspects AEME package include: Defined S4 class aeme objects Configuration models common standardised inputs Standardised calibration, manipulation visualisation

title: Introduction to AEME
text: aeme object main object AEME package. S4 class contains information required run model. aeme object contains following slots: lake - list object containing information lake (name, id, latitude, longitude, elevation, depth, area) time - list object containing information time (start, stop, spin_up, time_step) configuration - list object containing information configuration (model_controls, dy_cd, glm_aed, gotm_wet) observations - list object containing information observations (lake, level) inputs - list object containing information inputs (init_profile, init_depth, hypsograph, meteo, use_lw, Kw) inflows - list object containing information inflows (data, factor) outflows - list object containing information outflows (data, outflow_lvl, factor) water_balance - list object containing information water balance configuration (use, method, data) parameters - data.frame describing parameters input column names (model, file, name, value, min, max, module, group) output - list object containing information outputs (n_members)

title: Introduction to AEME
text: lake slot contains information lake. list object contains following objects: name - Name lake (character). id - Lake ID (character numeric). latitude - Latitude lake (numeric). provided, latitude calculated centroid shape. longitude - Longitude lake (numeric). provided, longitude calculated centroid shape. elevation - Elevation lake (numeric). shape - Shape lake (sf object). shape lake can represented polygon. centroid polygon used calculate latitude longitude lake. depth - Max depth lake (m) (numeric). Depth area used generate simple hypsographic curve none provided inputs slot. area - Surface area lake (m2) (numeric) Objects bold required building running model.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: time slot contains information time. list object contains following objects: start - Start date simulation (character). start date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. stop - End date simulation (character). end date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. timestep - Timestep simulation (numeric). timestep must seconds. spin_up - List spin periods simulation model (numeric). spin period must days. spin period period time model run simulation period. spin period used initialise model discarded examining simulation period.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: configuration slot list contains model configurations. includes configurations files hydrodynamic components well aquatic ecosystem model components: Files hydrodynamic ecosystem models. build_aeme() ran, model_controls data.frame passed function argument added configuration slot. details model_controls, see ’s section .

title: Introduction to AEME
text: observations slot list contains observations -lake (lake) variables (e.g. water temperature, chlorophyll-, dissolved oxygen etc.) water level (level). observations used assess model performance using function also calibrate model using aemetools package. lake observations stored data frame following columns: Date - Date observation (character). date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. depth - Depth observation (m) (numeric). depth must metres. var - Variable name observation (character). variable names input preparation designed AEME inputs article. value - Value observation (numeric). level observations stored data frame following columns: Date - Date observation (character). date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. value - Value observation (numeric). value must metres sea level within range hypsograph elevations.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: input slot list contains following objects: init_profile - profile initialise lake simulation (data.frame). columns: “depth”, “temperature” “salt”. provided, automatically generated using values model_controls. init_depth - depth lake initialising model (vector), provided, assume depth hypsograph. hypsograph - lake hypsograph. data.frame columns “elev”, “depth” “area”. data, can generate one using generate_hypsograph() function. meteo - meteorological data. data.frame minimum must contain columns date (“Date”), air temperature (“MET_tmpair), wind speed (”MET_wndspd”) shortwave radiation (“MET_radswd”). See AEME Inputs use_lw - Logical switch use longwave radiation. Defaults TRUE. Kw - light extinction coefficient (m−1m^{-1}).

title: Introduction to AEME
text: inflows slot list contains following objects: data - named list data.frames contain columns date (“Date”), flow (“HYD_flow”; m3day−1m^3 day^{-1}). Temperature can also provided (“HYD_temp”), however provided estimated using air temperature. name list used stream identifier model. method water_balance section set to3, “wbal” added data, contains separate inflow model, estimated using different evaporation functions inside model. factor - list scaling factors applied inflows. Named according model. inflows present slot empty.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: outflows slot list contains following objects: data - named list data.frames contain columns date (“Date”), flow (“HYD_flow”; m3day−1m^3 day^{-1}). method water_balance section set 2 3, “wbal” added data, contains separate outflow model, estimated using different evaporation functions inside model. factor - list scaling factors applied outflows. Named according model. However, can also passed parameter model_parameters section calibrated . preferred method applying scaling factors. elevation - named list elevations outflows occur. important falls within elevation range hypsograph. Set -1 outflow surface. outflows present slot empty.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: water balance slot generated internally build_aeme() function called wb_method set 2 3. slot contains: use: define lake level use. Can either observed (“obs”) modelled (“mod”) lake level. Default = “obs”. method: can 1 (inflows outflows) 2 (outflows calculated) 3 (inflows outflows calculated). default 2 . data: list two data.frames. “wbal” contains diagnostics estimating evaporation water balance model “model” contains modelled lake water level use “mod”.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: parameters slot contains data.frame parameters used building model. update default model parameters scale meteorological scale inflows outflows model. columns parameters data.frame : model - Either “dy_cd”, “glm_aed” “gotm_wet”. file - Either name file e.g. “glm3.nml” model specific files “met” meteorological variables “inf” inflow “wdr” outflows. (Outflows initiallly referred withdrawals, hence “wdr” notation, probably updated reflect current outflows slot soon…). name - Name parameter. name parameter nested nml/yaml file, whole hierarchy needs provide level separated “/” e.g. “light/Kw” Kw GLM-AED. value - Value parameter. min - Minimum range parameter. used aemetools::calib_aeme() aemetools::sa_aeme() function. max - Maximum range parameter. used aemetools::calib_aeme() aemetools::sa_aeme() function. group - Phytoplankton group. used GOTM-WET phytoplankton parameters. index - Index parameter. used GLM-AED parameters vectors e.g. sediment parameters (“sed_temp_mean”). module - Module parameter . necessary, helpful identifying parameters module GLM-AED GOTM-WET. function get_aeme_parameters() allows select parameters based model module. See ?get_aeme_parameters() details.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: output slot list updated run_aeme() executed. time executed, variable outputs designated model_controls added Aeme object.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: model_controls data.frame generated get_model_controls(). data.frame columns: var_aeme - character; AEME variable name simulate - logical; add variable Aeme object inf_default - numeric; default value use inflows none present inflows. particularly important configuring water chemistry inflows use_bgc = TRUE. initial_wc - numeric; value use initialising model. automatically updated variable present observations slot. initial_sed - numeric; value use initialising sediment module DYRESM-CAEDYM model. conversion_aed - numeric; factor multiply convert GLM-AED units. model built, model_controls data.frame stored configuration slot aeme object. can retrieved get_model_controls(aeme = aeme).

title: Introduction to AEME
text: aeme object can created using aeme_constructor() function. requires minimum lake, time, input list objects. object can also created YAML file using yaml_to_aeme() function. YAML file contains information required run model.

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: Reservoirs differ natural lakes several ways important hydrodynamic modelling: Regulated water levels – reservoir levels managed controlled releases rather natural outlet seepage. surface spillway activates reservoir near full capacity. penstock bottom outlet daily operational releases. mid-level selective withdrawal outlet water quality management (e.g. avoid releasing cold, anoxic hypolimnetic water). Thermal stratification management – withdrawals different depth layers affect downstream temperature water quality. AEME supports three major 1-D hydrodynamic models (DYRESM-CAEDYM, GLM-AED, GOTM-WET) multiple outlets arbitrary elevations. vignette walks setting reservoir ensemble model two outlets different levels: regulated penstock depth surface spillway.

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets

text: Meteorological data bundled AEME package (originally Lake Wainamu, North Island) reused drive reservoir simulation.

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: hypsograph describes relationship elevation surface area (thus volume). Constructed reservoirs typically prismatic (box-like) shape compared natural lakes. reflected higher volume_development parameter (values > 1.5 give convex, cylindrical shape; value 3 corresponds perfect cylinder).
code: hypsograph <- generate_hypsograph(   max_depth          = depth,   surface_area       = area,   volume_development = 2.5,   # more prismatic than a natural lake   elev               = elev,   ext_elev           = 2      # extend 2 m above full supply level )  head(hypsograph) #>    elev depth    area #> 1 152.0   2.0 1391324 #> 2 150.0   0.0 1200000 #> 3 149.8  -0.2 1176144 #> 4 149.6  -0.4 1152574 #> 5 149.4  -0.6 1129291 #> 6 149.2  -0.8 1106292 ggplot(hypsograph, aes(x = area / 1e6, y = elev)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#0065a9") +   geom_point(size = 1.5, colour = "#0065a9") +   labs(     x     = expression("Area (km"^2 * ")"),     y     = "Elevation (m a.s.l.)",     title = "Reservoir – hypsograph"   ) +   theme_bw()

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: create synthetic seasonal inflow time series typical New Zealand catchment, higher flows winter (June–August) lower flows summer. inflow data frame must contain minimum Date HYD_flow (m³ day⁻¹). Temperature (HYD_temp, °C) salinity (CHM_salt, PSU) columns recommended.
code: set.seed(42) sim_dates <- seq(as.Date("2020-01-01"), as.Date("2021-12-31"), by = "day") doy       <- as.integer(format(sim_dates, "%j"))  # Seasonal signal: peak winter flow ~day 200 (NZ Southern Hemisphere winter) inflow_flow <- pmax(5000,   80000 + 60000 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 200) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 8000))  # River temperature: coolest in winter, warmest in summer inflow_temp <- pmax(4, 15 - 8 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 15) / 365))  inflow_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = inflow_flow,   HYD_temp = inflow_temp,   CHM_salt = 0 )  head(inflow_data[, 1:3]) #>         Date HYD_flow HYD_temp #> 1 2020-01-01 33371.71 7.231200 #> 2 2020-01-02 17605.56 7.199484 #> 3 2020-01-03 24764.44 7.170079 #> 4 2020-01-04 26675.80 7.142995 #> 5 2020-01-05 24617.84 7.118239 #> 6 2020-01-06 20322.85 7.095819

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: key feature demonstrated vignette configuration two outlets different elevations: Visualise inflow outflows simulation period:  penstock provides near-constant regulated release throughout year, spillway flows high-flow winter months.
code: # Penstock: regulated base flow with small seasonal variation penstock_flow <- pmax(0,   60000 + 15000 * sin(2 * pi * (doy - 100) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 4000))  # Spillway: only active during the high-inflow winter period spillway_flow <- pmax(0,   25000 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 200) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 5000))  penstock_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = penstock_flow )  spillway_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = spillway_flow ) flows <- bind_rows(   mutate(inflow_data[, c("Date", "HYD_flow")], stream = "Inflow"),   mutate(penstock_data, stream = "Penstock (130 m)"),   mutate(spillway_data, stream = "Spillway (surface)") ) |>   filter(Date >= as.Date("2020-08-01"),          Date <= as.Date("2021-06-30"))  ggplot(flows, aes(x = Date, y = HYD_flow / 1e3, colour = stream)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c("Inflow"             = "#0065a9",                "Penstock (130 m)"   = "#d73027",                "Spillway (surface)" = "#4dac26"),     name = NULL   ) +   labs(     x     = "Date",     y     = expression("Flow (×10"^3 * " m"^3 * " day"^{-1} * ")"),     title = "Simulated inflow and outflow discharges"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

text: vignette shown configure AEME reservoir multiple outlets different elevations. key steps : Define reservoir geometry using prismatic hypsograph (volume_development > 1.5) appropriate constructed reservoir. Create time series inflow outlet independently. Register multiple outlets add_outflows(), providing named data list matching named elevation list. Use elevation = -1 surface outlet; provide actual elevation (m .s.l.) subsurface outlets, ensuring values fall within hypsograph elevation range. Build run model ensemble build_aeme() run_aeme(). Currently one three hydrodynamic models, GLM-AED, supported AEME (DYRESM-CAEDYM, GLM-AED, GOTM-WET) can handle multiple outlets produce separate outlet files build step, allowing outlet’s contribution tracked independently.

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: build_aeme() supports three water balance methods, selected via wb_method. right choice depends forcing data observations available. table summarises use :

what: Method 1 — Closed lake (no inflows or outflows)
title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: simplest assumption lake hydrologically isolated: volume changes driven direct precipitation lake surface evaporation . ΔVt=Pt⋅−Et⋅\Delta V_t = P_t \cdot A_t - E_t \cdot A_t ΔVt\Delta V_t change lake volume (m³/day), PtP_t precipitation depth (m/day), EtE_t evaporation depth (m/day), AtA_t lake surface area (m²) time tt. use: Good initial exploration, lakes without inflow gauges, want estimate evaporation component. -represent evaporation significant inflows keep lake warmer otherwise , -predict lake gains volume groundwater.  using GLM-AED model, default “spillway” lake level exceeds maximum elevation hypsograph. improve closed-lake assumption, useful merge bathymetry surrounding DEM get extended hypsograph. See bathytools article example.
code: model <- "glm_aed" path1 <- file.path(tempdir(), "rotoehu_wb1")  # Build and run model with Method 1 (closed lake) aeme_wb1 <- aeme |>   build_aeme(model = model, path = path1, wb_method = 1) |>   run_aeme(model = model, path = path1)  # Plot water level aeme_wb1 |>    plot_wbal_annual()

what: Method 2 — Outflow fitted from observed water levels
title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: lake-level observations available, AEME can optimise simple weir-type outflow rating curve simulated water level matches observations. outflow equation : Ot=C⋅max⁡(ht−hinv,0)1.5×86400O_t = C \cdot \max\!\left(h_t - h_{inv},\ 0\right)^{1.5} \times 86400 OtO_t outflow (m³/day), hth_t simulated water level (m sea level), hinvh_{inv} inversion height (m) — level outflow zero — CC outflow coefficient. CC hinvh_{inv} fitted minimising RMSE simulated observed water levels using estimate_lake_wlev(). lake-level observations available, method can used fit outflow parameters constant lake level initial lake depth. calibrated, fitted parameters can retrieved get_wbal_param() transferred different (e.g. ungauged) period set_wbal_param(). use: preferred method water-level gauge record exists. simultaneously constrains water balance provides physically meaningful outflow estimate. lake well-defined spillway outlet, fitted hinvh_{inv} often corresponds closely known sill elevation.
code: path2 <- file.path(tempdir(), "rotoehu_wb2")  aeme_wb2 <- aeme |>   build_aeme(model = model, path = path2, wb_method = 2) |>   run_aeme()  # Plot weir calibration results aeme_wb2 |>    plot_weir_calibration()

what: Method 3 — Inflow and outflow as residuals
title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: inflow water-level observations available (inflows estimated), Method 3 closes water balance partitioning daily residual effective inflow spill outflow: residualt=ΔVt−(Qin,t+PtAt−EtAt−Ot−St)\text{residual}_t = \Delta V_t - \left(Q_{,t} + P_t A_t - E_t A_t - O_t - S_t\right) positive residual (lake gains volume known fluxes explain) attributed unexplained inflow; negative residual attributed additional spill outflow. use: gauged inflows available water balance still close — example significant groundwater exchange ungauged catchment runoff suspected. Comparing residual time series across seasons flow events can help identify likely source discrepancy.
code: path3 <- file.path(tempdir(), "rotoehu_wb3")  aeme_wb3 <- aeme |>   build_aeme(model = model, path = path3, wb_method = 3) |>   run_aeme()

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: Evaporation depends strongly vapour pressure deficit water surface overlying air, turn depends lake surface temperature (TsT_s). AEME therefore estimates TsT_s computing evaporation.

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: exported function estimate_surface_temperature() integrates energy-balance model forward daily time steps: dTsdt=Qsw+Qlw+Qh+Qeρwcphmix\frac{dT_s}{dt} = \frac{Q_{sw} + Q_{lw} + Q_h + Q_e}{\rho_w\, c_p\, h_{mix}} Default parameters: shortwave albedo α=0.07\alpha = 0.07; bulk sensible/latent heat coefficients Ch=Ce=1.3×10−3C_h = C_e = 1.3 \times 10^{-3}; mixing fraction fmix=0.2f_{mix} = 0.2; relaxation timescale τrelax=3days\tau_{relax} = 3\,\text{days}.

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: measured surface temperatures (HYD_temp) present lake observations, predicted temperature observed timestep nudged toward observation using relaxation scheme: Ts(t+1)=Tspred+Δtτrelax(Tsobs−Tspred)T_s(t+1) = T_s^{pred} + \frac{\Delta t}{\tau_{relax}}\left(T_s^{obs} - T_s^{pred}\right) behaviour depends observation frequency: Frequent observations (weekly better): simulated surface temperature closely tracks lake. Evaporation observation-constrained reflects actual thermal state. Sparse observations (monthly seasonal): model fills gaps using energy balance, relaxing toward observation becomes available. Evaporation estimates observations carry uncertainty. observations: energy balance runs freely air-temperature seed. fall-back linear regression Ts=5+0.75T¯air,5dT_s = 5 + 0.75\,\overline{T}_{air,5\text{d}} (Stefan & Preud’homme, 1993) provides initial condition. can inspect estimated surface temperature model output variable:
code: plot_output(aeme_wb1, model = model, var_sim = "HYD_surft")

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: AEME uses bulk aerodynamic latent heat approach. Three now-exported functions implement physics step step, making easy inspect reproduce calculation independently.

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: saturation vapour pressure water surface computed Magnus formula: es(Ts)=exp⁡(2.3026×(7.5TsTs+237.3+0.7858))[hPa]e_s(T_s) = \exp\!\left(2.3026 \times \left(\frac{7.5\,T_s}{T_s + 237.3} + 0.7858\right)\right) \quad \text{[hPa]} exponential increase temperature warm lakes evaporate substantially cold ones even wind speed.
code: Ts_vals <- seq(0, 30, by = 5) es_vals <- sat_vapour_pressure(Ts_vals) data.frame(Ts_degC = Ts_vals, es_hPa = round(es_vals, 2)) #>   Ts_degC es_hPa #> 1       0   6.11 #> 2       5   8.72 #> 3      10  12.28 #> 4      15  17.05 #> 5      20  23.38 #> 6      25  31.67 #> 7      30  42.42

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: latent heat flux (W/m²) computed using bulk aerodynamic formula. evaporative heat loss retained (result capped zero condensation add water lake): Qlh=min⁡(0.622PCeρairLvU(ea−es),0)Q_{lh} = \min\!\left(\frac{0.622}{P}\,C_e\,\rho_{air}\,L_v\,U\,(e_a - e_s),\ 0\right) vapour pressure deficit (ea−es)(e_a - e_s) drives evaporation. warm surface raises ese_s, increasing deficit evaporative flux. High winds increase turbulent moisture transport.
code: # Example: 20 °C lake, 15 °C air, ~60 % relative humidity, 3 m/s wind Ts <- 20;  Ta <- 15;  U <- 3 ea <- 0.60 * sat_vapour_pressure(Ta)   # ~60 % RH Qlh <- latent_heat_flux(Ts = Ts, wndspd = U, prvapr = ea) cat(sprintf("Latent heat flux: %.1f W/m²\n", Qlh)) #> Latent heat flux: -93.1 W/m²

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: heat flux converted evaporation rate metres per day: E=QlhLvρw×86400[m/day]E = \frac{Q_{lh}}{L_v\,\rho_w} \times 86400 \quad \text{[m/day]}
code: E_m_day <- flux_to_evap(Qlh) cat(sprintf("Evaporation rate: %.4f m/day  (%.1f mm/day)\n",             E_m_day, E_m_day * 1000)) #> Evaporation rate: -0.0033 m/day  (-3.3 mm/day)

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: article demonstrated : Load refine lake data Lake Rotoehu using aemetools bathytools. Choose water balance method: Method 1 (closed lake): meteorology ; estimates evaporation residual precipitation volume change. Method 2 (fitted outflow): optimises weir-type rating curve (Ot=C⋅(ht−hinv)1.5O_t = C \cdot (h_t - h_{inv})^{1.5}) observed water levels; preferred method gauge record available. Method 3 (inflow + outflow residual): partitions unexplained storage changes effective inflows spill outflows; useful gauged inflows known budget still close. Understand surface temperature estimation: energy-balance model integrates forward time nudged toward observations via relaxation scheme (default τ=3days\tau = 3\,\text{days}). Without observations linear air-temperature regression seeds initial condition. Trace evaporation calculation three exported functions — sat_vapour_pressure(), latent_heat_flux(), flux_to_evap() — corresponding step bulk aerodynamic method. Visualise summarise evaporation using plot_output() (variable "LKE_evprte"), plot_est_wbal(), plot_wbal(), get_var().

Default: 0. wb_method integer; water balance method. One : 1 — inflows outflows 2 — outflows calculated (default) 3 — unexplained storage changes treated effective inflows/outflows model_controls data.frame; model configuration, typically loaded via get_model_controls(). inf_factor named numeric vector; factors multiply inflows , named model. outf_factor named numeric vector; factors multiply outflows , named model. calc_wbal logical; calculate water balance. Default: TRUE. coeffs numeric vector length 2; coefficients estimating surface water temperature calculating evaporation. water temperature observations present aeme, linear model fitted air temperature. One : 1 — relative humidity (%) 2 — wet-bulb temperature 3 — dew point temperature (default) 4 — specific humidity (kg/kg) est_swr_hr logical; estimate hourly shortwave radiation daily values. Default: TRUE. use_aeme logical; use aeme object generate model configuration files. Default: FALSE. config list; AEME configuration, typically loaded via yaml::read_yaml("aeme.yaml").

title: Estimate zone-specific sediment fluxes from hypsograph — estimate_zone_fluxes
text: aeme Aeme object. path character; directory input files located. Defaults path stored aeme, current working directory set. ref_depth Numeric. Reference depth (m) literature baseline fluxes. Default 5. baseline Named numeric vector baseline fluxes ref_depth. Must include fsed_oxy, fsed_amm, fsed_nit, fsed_frp. verbose Logical. Print zone summary copy-paste config lines. Default TRUE.

title: Estimate zone-specific sediment fluxes from hypsograph — estimate_zone_fluxes
text: Invisibly returns named list following elements: fsed_oxy Numeric vector length n_zones. Sediment oxygen demand flux (mmol O2/m2/d, negative). fsed_amm Numeric vector length n_zones. Ammonium flux (mmol N/m2/d). fsed_nit Numeric vector length n_zones. Nitrate flux (mmol N/m2/d). fsed_frp Numeric vector length n_zones. Filterable reactive phosphorus flux (mmol P/m2/d). zone_summary Data frame zone geometry final flux estimates. method Character string; either "baseline_scaled" "obs_adjusted".

title: Estimate zone-specific sediment fluxes from hypsograph — estimate_zone_fluxes
text: Tier 1 (always) — area-weighted depth scaling. zone's flux scaled literature baseline values according mean depth fractional bed area. Deep zones receive higher SOD nutrient fluxes reflecting greater organic matter accumulation persistent anoxia. Tier 2 (optional, obs supplied) — observed data adjustment. Near-bed summer concentrations O2, NH4, NO3, FRP used adjust relative difference fluxes zones. inter-zone ratios adjusted, absolute magnitude, lake-wide total preserved. Literature baselines reference depth 5 m (temperate lakes): fsed_oxy: -25 mmol O2/m2/d (Müller et al. 2012; Sondergaard et al. 2003) fsed_amm: 2 mmol N/m2/d (Andersen 1982; Beutel 2006) fsed_nit: 0.2 mmol N/m2/d (Seitzinger 1988) fsed_frp: 0.05 mmol P/m2/d (Nürnberg 1984) Depth scaling (Beutel 2006; Müller et al. 2012): SOD NH4/FRP fluxes scale approximately linearly mean zone depth divided ref_depth. NO3 flux transitions small positive values (shallow, oxic) negative values (deep, anoxic denitrification) approximately 0.5 * max_depth.

text: data frame 452 rows 9 variables: module Character. configuration block (GLM) module (AED) parameter belongs . GLM modules correspond Fortran namelist blocks glm3.nml (e.g., "glm_setup", "mixing", "morphometry", "time", "output", "init_profiles", "light", "bird_model", "sediment", "snowice", "meteorology", "inflow", "outflow", "wq_setup"). AED modules correspond namelist blocks aed.nml (e.g., "aed_oxygen", "aed_nitrogen", "aed_phosphorus", "aed_silica", "aed_phytoplankton", "aed_sedflux", "aed_seddiagenesis"). group Character. optional sub-category grouping related parameters process function within module. example, "nitrification", "denitrification", "sediment_flux" within aed_nitrogen module; "radiation", "wind", "rainfall" within meteorology module. Empty string ("") sub-grouping applies. parameter Character. parameter name used configuration file (e.g., "max_layers", "Fsed_oxy", "R_nitrif"). label Character. short, human-readable label parameter (e.g., "Layers", "Sediment O2 flux", "Nitrification rate"). symbol Character. mathematical symbol used model documentation equations, rendered plain text (e.g., "N_MAX", "F_sed^oxy", "theta_nitrif"). Empty string symbol defined. description Character. description parameter, role model, relevant context. units Character. units parameter. Uses "-" dimensionless quantities, "string" text parameters, "boolean" logical switches. title: Parameter library for the GLM-AED model. — glm_aed_parameter_library
text: Parameters organised module (namelist block AED module belong ) optionally group (sub-category describing process context, "nitrification", "sediment_flux", "radiation"). GLM (General Lake Model) parameters configure hydrodynamic model, including layer structure, mixing, morphometry, meteorological forcing, boundary conditions (inflows outflows), light penetration, ice/snow dynamics, sediment heat exchange. AED (Aquatic EcoDynamics) parameters configure water quality biogeochemical modules couple GLM. modules included dataset cover dissolved oxygen, inorganic nitrogen (ammonium, nitrate, nitrification, denitrification), inorganic phosphorus (phosphate, adsorption), silica, phytoplankton (growth, light, nutrient uptake, respiration, mortality, settling), sediment biogeochemistry (static sediment fluxes via aed_sedflux dynamic diagenesis via aed_seddiagenesis). Note aed_phytoplankton parameters listed groups "growth", "light", "nitrogen", "phosphorus", "silica" per-phytoplankton-group parameters typically specified separate phyto_data namelist file rather directly aed.nml.

title: Load model configuration to the aeme object — load_configuration
text: aeme Aeme object. model character vector; models use. One "dy_cd", "glm_aed", "gotm_wet". Defaults models found aeme. path character; directory input files located. Defaults path stored aeme, current working directory set. model_controls data.frame; model configuration, typically loaded via get_model_controls(). use_bgc logical; enable biogeochemical model. Default: FALSE. ext_elev numeric; elevation (m) extend hypsograph . Default: 0. calc_wbal logical; calculate water balance. Default: TRUE. wb_method integer; water balance method. One : 1 — inflows outflows 2 — outflows calculated (default) 3 — unexplained storage changes treated effective inflows/outflows calc_wlev logical; calculate water level. Default: TRUE. use_aeme logical; use aeme object generate model configuration files. Default: FALSE. coeffs numeric vector length 2; coefficients estimating surface water temperature calculating evaporation. water temperature observations present aeme, linear model fitted air temperature. Otherwise defaults \(T_{water} = 5 + 0.75 \times T_{air}\) (Stefan & Preud'homme, 1993, doi:10.1111/j.1752-1688.1993.tb01502.x ). hum_type integer; humidity input type GOTM. One : 1 — relative humidity (%) 2 — wet-bulb temperature 3 — dew point temperature (default) 4 — specific humidity (kg/kg) est_swr_hr logical; estimate hourly shortwave radiation daily values. Default: TRUE.

text: functions provide unified interface running external hydrodynamic biogeochemical lake models within R. function moves appropriate simulation directory, executes model's command-line binary, prints progress messages, reports whether model run completed successfully. functions intended called side effects: return model results directly, instead produce model output files simulation folder.

code: run_dy_cd(   sim_folder,   verbose = FALSE,   debug = FALSE,   args = character(),   timeout = Inf )  run_glm_aed(   sim_folder,   verbose = FALSE,   debug = FALSE,   args = character(),   timeout = Inf )  run_gotm_wet(   sim_folder,   verbose = FALSE,   debug = FALSE,   args = character(),   timeout = Inf )

title: Run AEME models — run_dy_cd
text: sim_folder directory simulation files contained verbose Logical: output model shown debug Logical; save debug file. DYRESM . args character vector additional command-line arguments pass model executable. Currently used GLM-AED. Options : "–xdisp" plot model output using plots.nml settings. timeout timeout seconds, ignored 0.  limit     elapsed time running command separate process.   Fractions     seconds ignored.

title: Run AEME models — run_dy_cd
text: Invisibly returns NULL.

title: Run GLM-AED diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics
text: Run GLM-AED diagnostics

title: Run GLM-AED diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics
code: run_glm_aed_diagnostics(   aeme,   model,   groups = NULL,   depth_collapse = "mean",   plot = FALSE,   use_bounds = TRUE,   print_table = TRUE )

title: Run GLM-AED diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics
text: model Model name. One "gotm_wet", "glm_aed", "dy_cd". groups character vector selecting catalogue entries. Accepts: catalogue entry names (e.g. "nitrogen_state"), element codes ("O","N","P","Phy"), types ("state","process"). Default NULL = entries. depth_collapse "mean", "surface" "max" — reduce 3D variables plot draw combined plots, grouped element use_bounds add dashed lines plots showing expected bounds (catalogue) print_table print kable summary

title: Run GLM-AED diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics
text: invisibly, list(summary, plots, data)

title: AEME 0.3.1
text: get_config_value() — retrieve configuration value Aeme object, falling back package defaults set. get_wbal_param() — retrieve fitted water-balance outflow parameters (C h_inv) stored Aeme object. set_wbal_param() — store water-balance outflow parameters Aeme object use subsequent build_aeme() calls. plot_output_base() — new base-R plotting function AEME model output, producing heatmap-style depth–time plots without ggplot2 dependency. Can also invoked via plot_output(..., backend = "base"). get_mean_sea_level_pressure() — utility function convert station pressure mean sea level pressure given air temperature elevation. get_station_pressure() — inverse get_mean_sea_level_pressure(); converts mean sea level pressure back station pressure.

title: AEME 0.3.1
text: plot_output() — new backend argument ("ggplot2" "base") selects plotting engine. Also improved variable/model availability checks: models variables missing output now warned dropped gracefully rather erroring. run_aeme() / run_glm_aed() — new args parameter passes additional command-line arguments model executable (e.g. "--xdisp" display GLM plots using plots.nml settings run). build_glm() — automatically copies bundled plots.nml template GLM simulation directory one already present. build_aeme() — model path now resolved Aeme configuration supplied arguments. build_aeme() arguments default config_defaults() specified. estimate_zone_fluxes() — output table now rendered using clitable cleaner formatted console display; documentation expanded method description, depth-scaling references, full description return value. initialise_aed() — informative message now shown initialisation value differs meaningfully replaced default. initialise_glm() — added guard required init_profiles fields (wq_names, num_wq_vars, wq_init_vals) may absent older NML files. set_glm_aed_models() — messaging improved AED sub-models removed. run_glm_aed_diagnostics() — plot argument now defaults FALSE. calc_water_balance() / estimate_lake_wlev() / estimate_surface_temperature() / standardise_inflow() / build_glm() — console messaging overhauled using new cli_safe() internal helper, respects AEME.inform option supports indented output. Missing inflow state variables now reported filled default values rather generic warning. clitable moved Suggests Imports; knitr moved Imports Suggests; psychrolib removed Imports (psychrometric calculations now handled internally via get_mean_sea_level_pressure() / get_station_pressure()).

title: AEME 0.3.1
text: Fixed variable naming DY-CD model output (read_dy_output(), read_model_outputs()). Removed pH default model controls (get_model_controls()). Simplified corrected variable-name look-ups lake_obs_to_aeme(), read_dy_output(), read_glm_output(), read_gotm_output(), read_model_outputs() use updated key_naming$var_aeme column. Removed now-redundant internal helper format_model_vars_vec(); behaviour folded get_model_vars(as_vector = TRUE). Fixed initialisation guard initialise_FABM(), initialise_aed(), initialise_glm() — empty model-controls tables now return early informative message rather erroring. Fixed CLI bug estimate_lake_wlev(). Fixed typo bug estimate_zone_fluxes() column-renaming step (dplyr::case_match replaced dplyr::recode compatibility).

title: AEME 0.2.0
text: AEME S4 object overhaul — Aeme S4 class substantially refactored: accessor/replacement generics simplified slot structure updated consistency. build_aeme() — major refactor; improved handling precipitation, inflows, outflows, lake-level initialisation. calc_fairall() — vectorised performance-improved implementation Fairall bulk aerodynamic algorithm. calc_water_balance() — refactored water-balance calculation; improved precipitation evaporation handling. calc_lake_obs_deriv() — extended compute additional derived observation variables. expand_met() — improved meteorological gap-filling unit conversion logic. load_output() — now dispatches new unified read_model_outputs() functions. check_aeme_vars(), check_glm_nml() — improved validation logic error messages. check_time() — robust time-period validation. print() / show() / summary() — AEME object print methods migrated use cli formatted console output. Inflow/outflow handling — new auto-detection column names units via standardise_inflow() guess_aeme_vars(); add_inflows() add_outflows() updated accordingly. Rain snow units — standardised mm/day throughout package. GLM NML helpers — new tests improved handling sediment parameters zone detection. GOTM YAML — new check_gotm_yaml() validates GOTM configuration model run. AED initialisation — initialiseAED() replaced initialise_aed(); library name spelling corrected “Ecodynamics”. GLM binaries — bundled GLM-AED binaries removed inst/extbin/; users now provide executable use glmtools package option. Parameter library — internal parameter library (bc2e234) get_aeme_params() updated include new parameters. pkgdown site — favicon assets extra CSS added; GLM-AED vignette registered. Removed deprecated nc_listify() internal helper. Updated Roxygen documentation v8 conventions throughout.
